summary.text: A 10-year-old girl with autism spectrum disorder due to AUTS2 deficiency and ADHD, treated with lisdexamfetamine, had severe persistent obstructive sleep apnea after adenotonsillectomy. Several CPAP attempts failed, with continuous use under 1 hour. Drug-induced sleep endoscopy showed palatine velum obstruction, septal dysmorphism and a bulky tongue base without adenoids.

A 4-week trial of atomoxetine and oxybutynin was started with the family. She received atomoxetine 25 mg with oxybutynin 5 mg in the first week and, after a phone call to assure adherence and tolerability, atomoxetine 60 mg with oxybutynin 5 mg. Her BMI was 26.1 kg/m^(2). A psychiatric and/or psychological evaluation preceded initiation.

Polysomnography showed a great improvement in AHI, a reduction of 72%, from 30.4 to 8.6 events/h, with nadir oxygen saturation rising from 73% to 86% and no change in sleep architecture. Treatment was well tolerated apart from several days of self-limited abdominal discomfort and no interactions with lisdexamfetamine were observed. The patient and family were pleased with the improvement.

summary.text: A 14-year-old adolescent girl with obesity (BMI 31.2 kg/m^(2)) and asthma presented with persistent OSA following adenotonsillectomy. Preoperative polysomnography showed non-optimal REM saturations of 90–93%, poorly controlled asthma and antihypertensive use; after AT the antihypertensive was no longer required but obesity worsened and asthma control stayed suboptimal.

CPAP was initially well tolerated for a year, then became intermittent and was discontinued. Liraglutide was introduced when BMI reached 38 kg/m^(2), with a BMI reduction of −7 kg/m^(2), and was later stopped with CPAP, with no further weight loss. A 4-week atomoxetine plus oxybutynin trial gave 25 mg and 5 mg in week one, then 80 mg and 5 mg. A psychiatric and/or psychological evaluation preceded initiation.

Polysomnography demonstrated a marked improvement, with AHI reduced by over 50% and below 5 events/h; REM sleep duration was significantly reduced while overall sleep efficiency was good. Treatment was generally well tolerated apart from transient abdominal pain and a single episode of vomiting in the first week. She reported no insomnia, her school performance improved and the patient and family were pleased.

summary.text: A 15-year-old adolescent girl with morbid obesity (BMI 44.5 kg/m^(2)) presented with severe persistent OSA following adenotonsillectomy, with an AHI of 69 events/h and an oxygen nadir of 77%. Polysomnography at age 11 had led to CPAP, whose use stayed intermittent and then fell to zero. Awake endoscopy showed no adenoid regrowth and no tonsils.

A 4-week atomoxetine plus oxybutynin trial was undertaken after a psychiatric and/or psychological evaluation, with baseline AHI of 31.5 events/h. Initial dosing prescribed was atomoxetine 25 mg and oxybutynin 5 mg in the first week, but calls got no response and the family confirmed non-adherence the day before follow-up polysomnography.

Atomoxetine 80 mg and oxybutynin 5 mg were given before the follow-up polysomnography. There was no overall improvement in AHI (45.3 events/h), except for reductions in REM AHI, and sleep efficiency and REM duration decreased. The family reported difficulty ensuring consistent intake and felt unable to insist on nightly compliance.
